📖 How to use

  1. Enter your current balance, rate and years remaining on the loan.
  2. Enter the new rate, new term and estimated closing costs.
  3. Read your monthly savings and the break-even month instantly.

❓ Frequently asked questions

How is the break-even point calculated?

Divide your total closing costs by the monthly payment savings. The result is the number of months you must keep the new loan before the refinance pays for itself.

Does this include taxes and insurance?

This tool compares only principal and interest. Taxes, insurance and PMI are not included, so confirm with your lender whether those change with the refinance.

When is refinancing a good idea?

Generally refinancing makes sense if you plan to stay past the break-even month and the new payment is lower. If the new payment is higher or the break-even is beyond your planned stay, it usually does not pay off.
